name: foreground-wait
what: A full test run, a build, a long sleep or a watcher is refused in the foreground so it can go to the background while the agent keeps working.

faults.fault: The limit on named test files is raised from three to thirty, so a run over many files counts as short.
A call that asks for the background is no longer recognised, so it is judged as a foreground run.
The sleep threshold is raised to a day, so a long sleep passes.
A single named test file is no longer enough to count as a short run.
The PowerShell tool is no longer inspected, so a full test run passes there.
--watch=false is treated as a watcher and refused.
Playwright is judged by file extensions again, so a plain name filter such as checkout is refused.
A whole-folder word such as tests no longer counts as a full run, so npx playwright test tests passes.
Jest and Vitest runs are no longer checked, so a full run of either passes.
A :line suffix no longer makes a name a file, so node --test a.spec.ts:12 counts as a full run.
A shell variable no longer counts as a file, so node --test $f counts as a full run.
The braces of ${NAME} are read as a glob, so node --test ${D}/a.test.mjs counts as a full run.
A --test flag after the script counts as node's own, so a script with its own --test option is refused.
A value flag's value reads as the script, so node --import x --test passes as an ordinary script run.
An input redirection counts as a file, so node --test a.test.mjs </dev/null is refused.
